description: Default capability for the GameLib shell: core defaults plus the opener plugin (the shell.openExternal / steam:// parity path). Tauri v2 capabilities gate WEBVIEW->Rust IPC only; they are not consulted for Rust-side plugin API calls. The four app-defined relay commands (sidecar_invoke, sidecar_send, open_external, sidecar_store_snapshot) are registered via invoke_handler and do not require capability permissions. For the same reason the native file/folder picker (dialog.showOpenDialog parity, plan 30-03) needs NO dialog permission here: dispatch_rust_channel calls app.dialog().file() from Rust. Granting 'dialog:allow-open' would have exposed plugin:dialog|open directly to renderer JavaScript (including anything running in the store WebView surface) for zero benefit to the intended path — WR-03. notification:allow-is-permission-granted is the ONLY notification permission granted, and it is required, not optional: tauri-plugin-notification (added plan 33-04) auto-injects init-iife.js into every webview, which on non-Windows unconditionally invokes plugin:notification|is_permission_granted at load — without the grant that invoke is denied and crashes startup with an unhandled rejection. The full notification:default set is deliberately NOT granted (WR-03): real OS notifications go Rust-side via the notification_show relay (Rust plugin API calls bypass capabilities), and the frontend never uses window.Notification, so plugin:notification|notify / show / request_permission stay unexposed to the renderer. updater:default (plan 34-05) is required for the JS auto-update API surface (check()/downloadAndInstall()) added by tauri-plugin-updater; it is scoped to the plugin's own default command set, not a broader grant. shell:allow-execute is granted with an explicit allow-list entry scoped to ONLY {name: 'binaries/gamelib-sidecar', sidecar: true} (plan 34-05, T-34-09) -- this exposes execution of exactly the bundled sidecar externalBin to the webview's shell:default surface and nothing else; it deliberately does NOT grant an unscoped shell:allow-execute, which would let renderer JS launch arbitrary programs on the host. The twelve core:window:* grants (allow-minimize, allow-maximize, allow-toggle-maximize, allow-unmaximize, allow-close, allow-start-dragging, allow-set-fullscreen, allow-is-fullscreen, allow-is-maximized, allow-is-minimized, allow-set-decorations, allow-set-title-bar-style) and the one core:webview:* grant (allow-set-webview-zoom) (Phase 34.1 D-01/D-04) are the exact command set the renderer-side window chrome calls — getCurrentWindow().minimize()/maximize()/toggleMaximize()/unmaximize()/close()/startDragging()/setFullscreen()/isFullscreen()/isMaximized()/isMinimized()/setDecorations()/setTitleBarStyle() plus getCurrentWebview().setZoom() — and nothing more. allow-set-title-bar-style (gap cycle 1, plan 34.1-10, G4) is the macOS decoration mechanism applyFramelessDecorations uses in place of setDecorations, because setDecorations(false) strips the native traffic lights (UAT test 9); it is macOS-only and purely cosmetic, granting no filesystem, process or network reach — untrusted remote content rendered in the main window inherits it, and the worst it can do is change the host window's titlebar appearance, the same class of reach core:window:allow-set-decorations (already granted) carries. core:window:default was deliberately NOT granted wholesale: it was read directly from the installed tauri 2.11.5 crate's own generated permission reference and is a read-only getter set — it contains allow-is-fullscreen/allow-is-maximized/allow-is-minimized but none of the mutation commands (minimize, maximize, toggle-maximize, unmaximize, close, start-dragging, set-fullscreen, set-decorations). The three read grants are therefore re-granted explicitly here so that nothing in this capability is inherited implicitly — every command the renderer can reach is named on one line. setZoomFactor's underlying setZoom call is a webview-scoped API in Tauri v2, not window-scoped, which is why core:webview:allow-set-webview-zoom sits in a different permission namespace from the other twelve; core:webview:default does not include it. The load-bearing reason for this explicit list: this capability is scoped "windows": ["main"] and GameLib renders untrusted remote content inside that same window (the store-search surface today, the Humble login flow in Phase 34.4). Under Tauri there is no <webview> isolation boundary, so remote content in main inherits every grant listed here — the same hazard this description already names above when explaining why dialog:allow-open was refused (Phase 33 WR-03). core:webview:allow-create-webview-window (Phase 34.1 D-12) lets the main window's renderer create child WebviewWindows for createNewWindow (ProtonDB / AppleWiki / AreWeAntiCheatYet reference pages) and showAboutWindow. The capability remains scoped "windows": ["main"], so the child windows themselves -- labelled about and external-<n> -- match NO capability and therefore receive ZERO Tauri command access; this fail-closed default is deliberate and load-bearing, because createNewWindow loads renderer-supplied REMOTE content and Tauri provides no <webview> isolation boundary. Child labels must never be added to the windows array and no second capability file may be created for them. tauri-plugin-deep-link (Phase 35 plan 07, D-07) is registered in main.rs but is granted NO permission here, and the absence is deliberate rather than an oversight: its four commands (get_current, register, unregister, is_registered) are reachable only from renderer JavaScript, and GameLib never uses the JS bindings -- the shell subscribes to on_open_url and calls register_all() from Rust, and Rust-side plugin API calls bypass capabilities entirely, exactly as the opening paragraph of this description already states. Granting deep-link:default would expose plugin:deep-link|get_current -- which returns the gamelib:// URL the app was opened with -- to whatever is running in the main window, including the untrusted remote content this capability's scope warns about above, for zero benefit to the intended path. That is the same refusal, for the same reason, that dialog:allow-open received (WR-03). Unlike tauri-plugin-notification, tauri-plugin-deep-link injects no init script into any webview (its Builder sets no js_init_script), so there is no load-time invoke that a missing grant would break.
